text: Assumption 1 . The sets $X\subset\mathbb{R}^{n}$ and $Y\subset\mathbb{R}^{m}$ are nonempty, compact, and convex. The functions $f$ and $g$ are continuously differentiable on neighborhoods of their respective domains, and $\nabla f$ and $\nabla g$ are $L_{f}$ - and $L_{g}$ -Lipschitz continuous, respectively, on $C=X\times Y$ .

Definition 2 (Approximate KKT point) . For $w\in C$ and $\lambda\geq 0$ , define $\displaystyle\Phi_{\rho}^{\rm s}(w,\lambda)$ $\displaystyle\coloneqq\operatorname{dist}\!\left(0,\nabla f(w)+\lambda\nabla R{}(w)+N_{C}(w)\right),$ $\displaystyle\Phi_{\rho}^{\rm f}(w)$ $\displaystyle\coloneqq[R{}(w)]_{+},\qquad\Phi_{\rho}^{\rm c}(w,\lambda)\coloneqq|\lambda R{}(w)|.$ We call $w$ an $(\varepsilon_{s},\varepsilon_{f},\varepsilon_{c})$ -KKT point of ( 1 ) if there exists $\lambda\geq 0$ such that $\Phi_{\rho}^{\rm s}(w,\lambda)\leq\varepsilon_{s}$ , $\Phi_{\rho}^{\rm f}(w)\leq\varepsilon_{f}$ , and $\Phi_{\rho}^{\rm c}(w,\lambda)\leq\varepsilon_{c}$ . When the three tolerances equal $\varepsilon$ , we simply call $w$ an $\varepsilon$ -KKT point. The case $\varepsilon=0$ gives the standard KKT conditions.
Definition 3 (ENNAMCQ) . We say that ENNAMCQ holds for ( 1 ) if, for every $w\in C$ with $R{}(w)\geq 0$ , $0\notin\nabla R{}(w)+N_{C}(w).$

Theorem 6 (Outer-iteration complexity) . Suppose Assumption 1 and ENNAMCQ hold, and suppose that the inverse-penalty grid satisfies $\widehat{\gamma}_{t}\leq M_{\gamma}\widehat{\gamma}_{t+1}$ for some $M_{\gamma}>1$ and every $t\geq 0$ . Let $\{\mu_{k}\}$ be positive and nonincreasing with $\mu_{k}=\Theta((1+k)^{-r})$ for some $r\in(0,1)$ , and let $\{\zeta_{k}\}$ satisfy $\zeta_{k}\leq\bar{\zeta}\mu_{k}^{q}$ for some $\bar{\zeta}>0$ and $q>1/r$ . Let $\{w^{k}\}$ be generated by Algorithm 1 and, for each $k\geq 0$ , set $\widetilde{\lambda}_{k+1}\coloneqq\gamma_{k}^{-1}\phi_{\mu_{k}}^{\prime}(\widetilde{R}^{k+1})$ . Then, for every sufficiently large $K$ , there exists $\widehat{k}\in[\lceil K/2\rceil,K]$ such that $\displaystyle\Phi_{\rho}^{\rm s}(w^{\widehat{k}+1},\widetilde{\lambda}_{\widehat{k}+1})$ $\displaystyle=O\!\left(K^{-(1-r)/2}\right),\qquad\Phi_{\rho}^{\rm f}(w^{\widehat{k}+1})=O(K^{-r}),$ (10) $\displaystyle\Phi_{\rho}^{\rm c}(w^{\widehat{k}+1},\widetilde{\lambda}_{\widehat{k}+1})$ $\displaystyle=O(K^{-r}).$ Consequently, within $K=O\!\left(\max\left\{\varepsilon_{s}^{-2/(1-r)},\varepsilon_{f}^{-1/r},\varepsilon_{c}^{-1/r}\right\}\right)$ outer iterations, we obtain an $(\varepsilon_{s},\varepsilon_{f},\varepsilon_{c})$ -KKT point of the $\delta$ -relaxed Moreau-gap formulation ( 1 ).

Corollary 7 (Overall first-order complexity) . Suppose the conditions of Theorem 6 hold and, in addition, choose $\zeta_{k}=\Theta(\mu_{k}^{q})$ . Suppose each required Moreau subproblem is solved by projected gradient to objective-gap accuracy $\zeta_{k}$ . Let $B_{\rm ls}$ denote a uniform bound on the number of trial Moreau evaluations per outer iteration, with $B_{\rm ls}=1$ for Strategy I. Then the overall first-order/projection complexity of IVSP through outer iteration $K$ is $O\!\left(B_{\rm ls}\,K\log K\right).$ In particular, for the balanced choice $r=1/3$ , IVSP computes an $\varepsilon$ -KKT point of the $\delta$ -relaxed Moreau-gap formulation ( 1 ) with overall first-order/projection complexity $O\!\left(B_{\rm ls}\,\varepsilon^{-3}\log\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\right)=\widetilde{O}(\varepsilon^{-3}).$

Proposition 12 (Stationarity properties of the Moreau gap) . Suppose that $g(x,\cdot)$ is $\sigma$ -weakly convex and $\rho\sigma<1$ . Let $H_{\rho}$ and $\mathcal{F}_{\delta}$ be given by ( 35 ). Then, for every $(x,y)\in C$ , $H_{\rho}(x,y)\geq\frac{1-\rho\sigma}{2\rho}\|y-z_{\rho}(x,y)\|^{2}.$ (37) Moreover, $\operatorname{dist}\!\left(0,\nabla_{y}g(x,z_{\rho}(x,y))+N_{Y}(z_{\rho}(x,y))\right)\leq\frac{1}{\rho}\|y-z_{\rho}(x,y)\|\leq\sqrt{\frac{2H_{\rho}(x,y)}{\rho(1-\rho\sigma)}}.$ (38) In particular, $H_{\rho}(x,y)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad y=z_{\rho}(x,y)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 0\in\nabla_{y}g(x,y)+N_{Y}(y).$ (39) Hence, $\mathcal{F}_{0}=\{(x,y)\in C:y\in\widetilde{S}(x)\},$ (40) where $\widetilde{S}$ is given by ( 36 ).

Corollary 13 (Interpretation of approximate feasibility) . Let $w=(x,y)\in C$ satisfy $[R(w)]_{+}\leq\varepsilon_{f},$ where $R(w)=H_{\rho}(w)-\delta.$ Then $H_{\rho}(w)\leq\delta+\varepsilon_{f},$ and consequently $\displaystyle\|y-z_{\rho}(x,y)\|$ $\displaystyle\leq\sqrt{\frac{2\rho(\delta+\varepsilon_{f})}{1-\rho\sigma}},$ $\displaystyle\operatorname{dist}\!\left(0,\nabla_{y}g(x,z_{\rho}(x,y))+N_{Y}(z_{\rho}(x,y))\right)$ $\displaystyle\leq\sqrt{\frac{2(\delta+\varepsilon_{f})}{\rho(1-\rho\sigma)}}.$

Proposition 14 (Degeneracy of the exact Moreau-gap constraint) . Under Assumption 1 , NNAMCQ (equivalently, MFCQ), fails at every feasible point of the exact Moreau-gap formulation $H_{\rho}\leq 0$ . On the other hand, for every $\delta>0$ , the relaxed constraint $H_{\rho}\leq\delta$ admits a strictly feasible point.

Proposition 15 (Automatic ENNAMCQ without nonconstant affine segments) . Let $\delta>0$ , and suppose the standing smoothness assumptions hold. Fix $\bar{x}\in X$ . Suppose that $g(\bar{x},\cdot)$ is convex on $Y$ and satisfies ( 43 ). Then $0\notin\nabla R(\bar{x},y)+N_{C}(\bar{x},y)$ for every $y\in Y$ such that $R(\bar{x},y)\geq 0$ . Consequently, if ( 43 ) holds for every $x\in X$ , then ENNAMCQ holds on $X\times Y$ . In particular, if $g(x,\cdot)+\iota_{Y}$ is strictly convex for all $x\in X$ , then ENNAMCQ holds on $X\times Y$ .

Proposition 16 (ENNAMCQ for few-shot learning) . Let $T,m,p\in\mathbb{N}$ . For each task $i=1,\ldots,T$ , let $S_{i}=\{(u_{i,r},q_{i,r})\}_{r=1}^{n_{i}},$ with $q_{i,r}\in\{1,\ldots,m\}$ , be a finite support set. For fixed $x\in X$ and a finite dataset $D$ , let $F_{x,D}(u)\in\mathbb{R}^{p}$ denote the feature vector produced for $u$ by the shared feature extractor when its batch-dependent statistics are computed from $D$ . For each $i$ and $r$ , set $F_{i,r}(x)\coloneqq F_{x,S_{i}}(u_{i,r}).$ Let $(W_{i},b_{i})\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times p}\times\mathbb{R}^{m}$ be the task-specific linear classifier, and set $y=((W_{i},b_{i}))_{i=1}^{T}\in Y,$ where $Y\subseteq\prod_{i=1}^{T}(\mathbb{R}^{m\times p}\times\mathbb{R}^{m})$ is convex. Define $\ell(s,q):=\log\left(\sum_{j=1}^{m}e^{s_{j}}\right)-s_{q},$ for $s=(s_{1},\ldots,s_{m})\in\mathbb{R}^{m},$ and for all $y=((W_{i},b_{i}))_{i=1}^{T}\in Y,$ $g(x,y):=\frac{1}{T}\sum_{i=1}^{T}\frac{1}{n_{i}}\sum_{r=1}^{n_{i}}\ell\bigl(W_{i}F_{i,r}(x)+b_{i},q_{i,r}\bigr).$ Then, for every fixed $x\in X$ , $g(x,\cdot)$ is convex on $Y$ and satisfies ( 43 ). Consequently, ENNAMCQ holds for every $\delta>0$ .

Proposition 17 (ENNAMCQ for sample-reweighting models) . Suppose the standing assumptions hold. Let $X=[-M,M]^{n}$ and let $Y$ be a compact set. Suppose $g(x,y)=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\omega(x_{i})\ell_{i}(y),\qquad\omega\geq 0,\quad\omega^{\prime}>0\ \text{on }[-M,M],$ (49) where each $\ell_{i}$ is continuous on $Y$ . Define $D_{\ell}:=\max_{1\leq i\leq n}\left(\max_{y\in Y}\ell_{i}(y)-\min_{y\in Y}\ell_{i}(y)\right).$ If $\delta>\omega(-M)D_{\ell},$ then ENNAMCQ holds on $X\times Y$ .

Corollary 18 (ENNAMCQ for sigmoid-reweighted classification) . Let $M,B_{y}>0$ , $n,m,d,d_{h}\in\mathbb{N}$ , $X=[-M,M]^{n}$ , and let $u_{i}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}$ and $q_{i}\in\{1,\ldots,m\}$ , $i=1,\ldots,n$ . Let $\omega(t):=(1+e^{-t})^{-1}$ denote the sigmoid sample-weight function. For $y=(A,a,V,b)\in Y\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{d_{h}\times d}\times\mathbb{R}^{d_{h}}\times\mathbb{R}^{m\times d_{h}}\times\mathbb{R}^{m},$ define $h_{y}(u):=V\operatorname{sigm}(Au+a)+b,$ where $\operatorname{sigm}$ denotes the logistic sigmoid applied componentwise, and set $\ell_{i}(y):=\ell(h_{y}(u_{i}),q_{i}),$ where $\ell$ is defined in Proposition 16 . Suppose $Y$ is nonempty, compact and convex, and every component of $V$ and $b$ lies in $[-B_{y},B_{y}]$ , and let $g$ be given by ( 49 ). If $\delta>\bigl(2B_{y}(d_{h}+1)+\log m\bigr)/(1+e^{M}),$ then ENNAMCQ holds on $X\times Y$ .

Example 23 (Deterioration of the ENNAMCQ margin) . Let $X$ be any nonempty compact convex set, $Y=[-1,1]$ , and $g(x,y)=\frac{1}{2}y^{2}.$ Then $g$ is independent of $x$ , and for every $\rho>0$ , $z_{\rho}(y)=\frac{y}{1+\rho},\qquad H_{\rho}(y)=\frac{\rho}{2(1+\rho)}y^{2}.$ Thus, for $0<\delta<\rho/(2(1+\rho))$ , the region $R(y)=H_{\rho}(y)-\delta\geq 0$ is characterized by $|y|\geq\sqrt{\frac{2(1+\rho)\delta}{\rho}}.$ Moreover, $\nabla H_{\rho}(y)=\frac{\rho}{1+\rho}y.$ Since the two points satisfying $|y|=\sqrt{\frac{2(1+\rho)\delta}{\rho}}$ lie in the interior of $Y$ due to the choice of $\delta$ , their normal cones are $\{0\}$ . Consequently, the minimum in Lemma 21 is attained at these points, and $\eta_{\delta}=\sqrt{\frac{2\rho}{1+\rho}}\sqrt{\delta}.$ Hence $\eta_{\delta}=\Theta(\sqrt{\delta})\to 0$ as $\delta\downarrow 0$ .

Remark 28 (Lower-level interpretation) . The feasibility estimate ( 110 ) in Theorem 6 , together with Corollary 13 , shows that the returned iterate $w^{\widehat{k}+1}=(x^{\widehat{k}+1},y^{\widehat{k}+1})$ satisfies $H_{\rho}(w^{\widehat{k}+1})\leq\delta+O(K^{-r}),$ and consequently, its associated Moreau proximal point $z_{\rho}(w^{\widehat{k}+1})$ satisfies $\|y^{\widehat{k}+1}-z_{\rho}(w^{\widehat{k}+1})\|=O\!\left(\sqrt{\delta+K^{-r}}\right),$ and $\operatorname{dist}\!\left(0,\,\nabla_{y}g\!\left(x^{\widehat{k}+1},z_{\rho}(w^{\widehat{k}+1})\right)+N_{Y}\!\left(z_{\rho}(w^{\widehat{k}+1})\right)\right)=O\!\left(\sqrt{\delta+K^{-r}}\right).$ Thus, the returned $y$ -iterate is close to a point that is near-stationary for the lower-level problem. In particular, with $r=1/3$ and $K=O(\varepsilon^{-3})$ , both errors are $O(\sqrt{\delta+\varepsilon})$ .
